name: Herbert
bio: A young man described in December 1898 simply as Hylton's — 'Hylton is here with his boy Herbert'. Nothing else about him is on record here: not his surname, not his age, not a word of his own.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06. **NOT Herbert Tankard** ([[tankard]]), the Savoy pageboy of the 1895 plea, and **not Herbert Horne** ([[horne]]) - three unrelated Herberts, which is why he is filed under a bare first name. HE SURVIVES IN FOUR WORDS, 'his boy Herbert', and that possessive is the whole of the evidence. Compare [[joseph]], 'his little friend Joseph', and [[alphonse]], 'your little friend Alphonse', both on this same folio: the map now holds three young men described to Turner in the same possessive formula in one letter. THE FOLIO IS A CENSUS OF THE PARIS EXILE HOUSEHOLD in December 1898 and should be read as one: Sir John Ashton and his 'little friend' Joseph (both already on this map, connected on this same page), Turner's 'little friend' Alphonse, and Hylton with 'his boy' Herbert. Four young men in three sentences, all described to Wilde's closest correspondent in the same possessive formula.
